title: Buddy — taskbar icon option and a tighter click area

steps.headline: A new 'Show as' row lets you pick the floating buddy or a taskbar icon.
steps.changed: One row added under the on/off switch: Floating or Taskbar (it says Menu bar on a Mac). The line under the row explains the choice you picked.
steps.notice: If you change it while the buddy is on, it switches right away. The floating mascot goes and the icon appears, or the other way round. The row's summary reads 'On — in your taskbar' when the icon is picked.
steps.risk: The popup is one row taller. When the switch is off, picking a style only saves your choice for next time; nothing appears.

steps.path: Settings → Buddy Floater → Show as: Taskbar, then the icon next to your clock
steps.headline: Pick Taskbar, then click the buddy icon by your clock. Does the chat open there, with the buttons under it?
steps.changed: A separate test copy of the app with this change in it. Your own YouCoded is not touched.
steps.notice: Left-click opens and closes the chat. Right-click gives Open chat, Switch to floating buddy and Hide buddy. A red dot shows on the icon while a session needs you. On Linux the app can't ask where the icon is, so the chat always opens in the bottom-right corner.
steps.risk: The icon is the purple app buddy, not your theme's mascot, and it shows a red dot rather than his shocked face. It's a second window on your desktop; close it when you're done.

steps.path: Settings → Buddy Floater → Show as: Floating, then the mascot on your desktop
steps.headline: Click just above and beside the floating buddy. Does he now ignore those clicks, but still respond when you click his body?
steps.changed: Only his drawn body counts as him now, plus a few pixels of slack so his thin arms are still easy to grab. Before, the whole invisible square around him did.
steps.notice: Clicking the empty space above or beside him no longer opens the chat, starts a drag or pops him out of the screen edge. On Windows and Mac those clicks also reach whatever is behind him.
steps.risk: On your Linux laptop those clicks still won't reach the window underneath (Linux can't let clicks through part of a window), so they just do nothing now.
